title: Severe bleeding
version: ANZCOR Guideline 9.1.1 'First Aid for Management of Bleeding' (Approved April 2021, supersedes July 2017; with 'Editorial Update - July 2025' on tourniquets); Hato Hone St John 'Bleeding' first aid library page (no date shown, footer 2025); Healthify He Puna Waiora 'Bleeding first aid' (Last reviewed 09 Jun 2026); all read 20 Nov 2026
sourceNote: Every site blocks direct download here (curl refused for anzcor.org, stjohn.org.nz, resus.org.au and copies on other sites) and web search gave titles only, so every line was read by a fetch tool asked to quote exact lines (long sentences in pieces, rejoined; curly apostrophes and quotes written straight). No PDF was in sources/. Sections: A ANZCOR 9.1.1 (main source, joint Australia-NZ; A1 summary, A2 recommendations, A3 external bleeding and when to treat as life-threatening, A4 management, A5 direct pressure, A6 embedded objects, A7 arterial tourniquet, A8 haemostatic dressings, A9 internal and closed limb bleeding, A10 nose bleed, A11 all severe bleeding, A12 July 2025 editorial update on tourniquets; the 1.6 flow chart is an image with no text and could not be captured; references, abbreviations and evidence background left out; tourniquet time and do-not-remove lines confirmed in two reads). B Hato Hone St John NZ 'Bleeding' (whole first-aid text; no tourniquet page found). C Healthify NZ 'Bleeding first aid' (cites St John and ANZCOR; nosebleed steps not captured; one line's opening words missing, marked). ANZCOR 9.2.3 (shock, Approved December 2025) was checked but has no shock-specific steps, so is not copied. Differences: (1) Raising the limb: St John (severe and minor bleeding, amputation) and Healthify (amputation; raise legs slightly for internal bleeding) say raise it; ANZCOR says there is no evidence elevating helps and it may cause more pain or injury, and instead says immobilise the limb. (2) Tourniquets and haemostatic dressings: only ANZCOR covers them (only for life-threatening limb bleeding not controlled by pressure, if trained and one is available; 5 cm above the bleeding point if no maker's instructions; not over a joint, wound or clothing; never covered; second one above the first; note the time and tell paramedics; do not remove until specialist care). St John and Healthify say only keep pressing. (3) Soaked-through padding: St John says keep pressing until the ambulance arrives; Healthify says add more padding and don't keep lifting it; ANZCOR says add a second pad and tighter bandage, then check position and possibly remove pads, and warns against layering more pads. (4) Embedded objects: ANZCOR and Healthify say do not remove (no size exception); St John says remove small ones near the surface (nail, staple) and do not remove large ones. (5) Amputated part: St John says keep it dry in a sealed bag in water and ice; Healthify says seal with a little air in cold water with ice cubes; ANZCOR only says an amputation above wrist or ankle is life-threatening bleeding, with no care of the part. (6) Nosebleed: St John 10 to 20 minutes, call 111 if not stopped after 20 minutes or after head injury; ANZCOR at rest at least 10 minutes, at least 20 minutes on a hot day or after exercise, seek medical help after 20 minutes. (7) Shock: ANZCOR gives signs (pale and sweaty plus pulse over 100, capillary refill over 2 seconds, reduced consciousness) and says 'treat shock' by reference only; Healthify lists signs and says call 111; St John does not use the word. (8) Food and drink: ANZCOR and Healthify say nothing by mouth for severe bleeding; St John only for internal bleeding. (9) St John and Healthify cover a head injury and skull fracture differently (Healthify: don't press if a skull fracture is possible). Gaps: no source says how many minutes to press on a wound (only until it stops or help arrives); none says what to do if no tourniquet training or kit beyond pressure and dressing; ANZCOR's 2025 update mentions possible harm after more than 2 hours of tourniquet use but keeps the advice unchanged and gives first aiders no action for long waits; no source says how to write the time (on the tourniquet or the person).
status: Reviewer: 3 instructions missed (keep wound edges together, consent, part kept dry) and 11 findings, all fixed but 4 gaps the sources leave open. 134 of 134 quotes exact (web copy).
